sec: Phases of chronic HBV: table rows, phase I-V, acute HBV vs chronic hepatitis phase IV

items.q: The p1040 phase table is built on marker rows. Which is NOT one of the printed row labels?
items.exp: Printed row labels are HBeAg, Anti-HBe, HBV DNA (and ALT); anti-HBs is not a row label here. (Book p1040)

items.q: Match the phase to the immune state printed under it — 1) Phase I 2) Phase II … A) Immune clearance B) Immune tolerant
items.exp: Phase I is labelled 'Immune tolerant', Phase II 'Immune clearance'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Fill up: Phase I is 'HBeAg positive ______ infection', lasting ______ years.
items.exp: 'Phase I / HBeAg Positive chronic infection : · 10 - 30 years'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Judge Phase I: I HBsAg and HBeAg are both positive with HBV DNA markedly raised. II ALT is normal, so the page concludes no treatment.
items.exp: Phase I prints 'HBsAg +ve', 'HBeAg +ve', 'HBV DNA ↑↑' and 'ALT : Normal → No [treatment]'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Which phase is captioned the 'optimal treatment time'?
items.exp: Phase II carries 'Optimal treatment time'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Match the phase to its descriptor — 1) Phase II 2) Phase III … A) Inactive carrier state B) Mildly symptomatic chronic hepatitis with ALT ↑↑
items.exp: Phase II: 'chronic hepatitis : · mildly Symptomatic … ALT ↑ ↑'. Phase III: 'Inactive carrier state'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Phase III (HBeAg-negative chronic infection) is qualified by which population note?
items.exp: 'Phase III / HBeAg Negative chronic infection : · majority population'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Fill up: in Phase III, HBeAg is ______ and HBV DNA is at its ______.
An HBeAg-negative patient presents like acute hepatitis — fever, malaise, vomiting, raised serum bilirubin and raised liver enzymes. Which phase does the page label this as?
opts: Phase IV — HBeAg negative chronic hepatitis
Phase I — HBeAg positive chronic infection
items.exp: Phase IV is 'HBeAg Negative chronic hepatitis' with 'Presentation — Acute symptoms : Fever, malaise, Vomiting' and 'Laboratory features : ↑ s. bilirubin, ↑ liver enzyme'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Phase IV presentation — match — 1) Symptoms 2) Laboratory … A) ↑ s. bilirubin, ↑ liver enzyme B) Fever, malaise, vomiting
items.exp: 'Presentation — Acute symptoms : Fever, malaise, Vomiting'; 'Laboratory features : ↑ s. bilirubin, ↑ liver enzyme'. (Book p1040)

items.q: What is printed for Phase V (HBsAg negative)?
opts: Chronic infection with no inflammation and minimal fibrosis
Chronic hepatitis with severe inflammation and cirrhosis
Inactive carrier state with high HBV DNA
items.exp: 'Phase V / HBsAg negative : chronic infection : · No inflammation · minimal fibrosis'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Which finding is NOT printed under Phase V (HBsAg negative)?
items.exp: Phase V prints 'chronic infection', 'No inflammation' and 'minimal fibrosis' only. (Book p1040)

items.q: A patient looks like acute hepatitis B, but you suspect it is really chronic hepatitis phase IV. Which test does the page print to settle it?
items.exp: The left block prints 'Acute hepatitis B — Anti HBc IgM +ve'. (Book p1040)

items.q: In the 'Chronic hepatitis phase IV' block, what quantitative HBsAg cut-off is printed for confirmation?
items.exp: 'For confirmation : · quantitative HBs Ag ( > 1000 IU/mL)'. (Book p1040)

items.q: Which is NOT one of the three items printed under 'For confirmation' in the chronic hepatitis phase IV block?
items.exp: The block lists quantitative HBsAg > 1000 IU/mL, 'Severely Symptomatic' and 'Very high HBV DNA load'; anti-HBc IgM belongs to the acute hepatitis B block. (Book p1040)

items.q: Judge the two bottom blocks: I Acute hepatitis B is confirmed by anti-HBc IgM positivity. II Chronic hepatitis phase IV is confirmed by quantitative HBsAg above 1000 IU/mL.
items.exp: Left block: 'Acute hepatitis B — Anti HBc IgM +ve'. Right block: 'Chronic hepatitis phase IV : For confirmation : · quantitative HBs Ag ( > 1000 IU/mL)'. (Book p1040)
